# Unit test for function check_dict_case
def test_check_dict_case():
    # Empty dictionary -> False
    assert check_dict_case({}) == False

    # Single lowercase / uppercase keys -> True
    assert check_dict_case({"a": 1}) == True
    assert check_dict_case({"A": 1}) == True

    # All lowercase keys -> True
    assert check_dict_case({"a": 1, "b": 2, "c": 3}) == True

    # All uppercase keys -> True
    assert check_dict_case({"A": 1, "B": 2, "C": 3}) == True

    # Mixed case violation on second key -> False
    assert check_dict_case({"a": 1, "B": 2, "c": 3}) == False
    assert check_dict_case({"A": 1, "b": 2, "C": 3}) == False

    # Non-string keys -> False
    assert check_dict_case({"a": 1, 2: 3}) == False
    assert check_dict_case({1: "a"}) == False
    assert check_dict_case({None: 1}) == False

    # Keys with no letter case (digits, symbols, empty string) -> False
    assert check_dict_case({"a1": 1}) == False
    assert check_dict_case({"1a": 1}) == False
    assert check_dict_case({"": 1}) == False
    assert check_dict_case({"Name": "John"}) == False

    # Uppercase keys containing digits still count as upper -> True
    assert check_dict_case({"STATE": "NC", "OID": "32"}) == True

    # Lowercase keys mixed with uppercase -> False
    assert check_dict_case({"p": "pineapple", "B": "banana"}) == False

    print("All tests passed!")
